claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` instead of the resolved value.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" for update conflicts.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
On Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs.
The Pulumi CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports limiting operations to specific resources with `--target` and `--exclude` flags.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide access to bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Converting a Pulumi output value to a string directly (concatenating or logging) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message.
In TypeScript, converting an Output to a string produces text containing `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling JSON.stringify() on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string yields text containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to json.dumps() fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; Output.json_dumps() should be used instead.
In Go, passing a pulumi.StringOutput where a string is expected is a compile error.
In C#, converting an Output to a string produces text containing `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting environment variable PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true (TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.
String-composition helpers: pulumi.interpolate and pulumi.concat in TypeScript; Output.concat/Output.format/Output.json_dumps in Python; pulumi.Sprintf/pulumi.JSONMarshal in Go; Output.Format in C#.
The apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name cannot accept an output.

In dynamically typed languages an `if` on an Output evaluates the output object and is generally always true; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error because Output<bool> is not bool.
Values known at program start, such as stack config read with pulumi.Config, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name, or loop bound/map key, fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (range(some_output)) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an Output; awaiting or reading it synchronously fails to compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. res.Outputs in Go).
Cross-references to docs pages exist: inputs-outputs, apply, all, stacks#stackreferences, automation-api.
